coreIdea: DFS=deep-first (stack/recursion). BFS=level-by-level (queue), gives shortest path in unweighted graphs. Undirected DFS: only tree+back edges.
mustRememberFormulas: O(V+E) adjacency list; O(V²) adjacency matrix
Tree edges in forest = n - c (c=connected components)
Back edge: d[v]<d[u]<f[u]<f[v] (v is ancestor). Forward: d[u]<d[v]<f[v]<f[u] (v is descendant)
Undirected graph DFS: NO forward/cross edges possible, only tree+back

commonTrapsQuickList: DFS tree does NOT give shortest paths — only BFS does
Undirected graphs: no forward/cross edges in DFS, only tree/back
Adjacency matrix forces O(V²) regardless of actual sparsity
BFS gives single-source shortest path, not all-pairs
highYieldPyqLessons: Edge classification/structural properties (11/23) is by far the dominant skill — master the discovery/finish-time interval rules cold, and remember the undirected-graph simplification.
This topic is the direct foundation for MST (Prim's) — the traversal skeleton (visit, mark, explore neighbors) is identical.
